extracted.intended_audience: journal editors, production staff, and authors preparing manuscripts for Sage journals
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and production requirements for preparing and transmitting final manuscripts and related materials for publication in Sage journals, and for managing issue-level production (TOC, page budgets, supplements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript file format
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscript must be submitted as a Word file (.doc or .docx) or TeX file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the accepted editable file formats for the main manuscript file; figures and other assets are expected as separate files where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conformity to journal/style guide
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscript must conform to the appropriate style throughout (APA, AMA, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure consistent formatting and citation style per the journal's required style before submission to production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final version readiness
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit the final version for publication, with developmental editing completed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Production expects the manuscript to be final — do not send drafts requiring further developmental edits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article metadata included
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscript must include title, short title, abstract, and keywords.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide these elements clearly in the manuscript to support indexing, metadata creation, and TOC entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete author information
rubrics_metrics.description: Include names, e-mails, affiliations, degrees, and biographies for ALL authors and a mailing address for the corresponding author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide full contact and biographical details for each author to ensure accurate publication and correspondence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author name formatting consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: Display author names and surnames correctly and in a manner consistent with previous publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure name order, diacritics, and surname handling match prior publications to avoid indexing errors and author identification issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article type or section heading
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscript must include article type or issue section heading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly label the manuscript (e.g., Research Article, Review, Editorial) to assist editors and production routing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Callouts for figures, tables, supplements
rubrics_metrics.description: Include callouts within article text for all figures, tables, and supplements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mark where each figure/table/supplement should appear; ensure callouts are present for production layout.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editable equations and chemical formulas
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not contain equations in image format — all math equations and chemical formulas must be editable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit equations in native, editable formats (MathType/TeX) rather than raster images to preserve quality and allow typesetting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete and consistent references
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes references for all in-text citations, and all references are mentioned in the text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-check citations and reference list to avoid missing or extraneous references; production expects a one-to-one correspondence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tables must be editable and properly placed
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not contain tables in image format — tables must be editable and should be submitted in Word, Excel, or PowerPoint, include captions, and be placed after the reference list in separate files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editable tables allow proper typesetting and indexing; place as requested to streamline production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figures submitted separately and meet artwork guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Contains figures submitted in their original format, preferably as separate files. Figures must meet Artwork Guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide figures separately (not embedded) in the original high-quality formats required by the journal; follow the Artwork submission page for detailed specs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental material formatting and labeling
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes properly formatted supplemental material. Supplemental Material can be in any file format and must be labeled "Online_supp."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplemental files are not edited by Sage or reviewed by the author prior to publication; they should be final, publish-ready files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissions for copyrighted material
rubrics_metrics.description: Include permission(s) for usages of copyrighted material as appropriate (signed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide signed permissions for third-party copyrighted materials to avoid legal/production delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Artwork resolution and file type requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures must be high resolution (at least 300 dpi). Line art should be submitted as vector-based (.eps) files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Raster images should be at or above 300 dpi; line art/vector graphics are preferred as EPS files to ensure print quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid embedding raster images in Word
rubrics_metrics.description: Images are best submitted separately from the text document. Do not embed raster image files in Word or similar programs as embedding reduces resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit image files separately to preserve original resolution; embedding can downsample images below acceptable print standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to issue production deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit all issue content (including the Table of Contents) by the deadlines provided by your Production Editor (PE).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meeting issue deadlines is imperative for on-time publication and can affect subscriptions and impact factor; include editorials, book reviews, and news pieces on schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use SMART Article List and TOC procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Use SMART’s Article List to review available articles for issue placement and for creating the Table of Contents; the PE can create the TOC for some journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SMART helps track submission dates, page counts, author names, and other data; discuss TOC creation options with the PE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain and submit editorial updates promptly
rubrics_metrics.description: Send updates for editorial boards, submission guidelines, and other recurring content as soon as possible; the deadline may be earlier than expected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use TOC preparation as a reminder for such updates and ask your PE for specific deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page budget awareness and management
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain awareness of your contractual number of pages allowed per volume and optimize acceptance and issue planning to stay within budget.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may divide the volume page budget among issues as desired; exceeding page budgets incurs costs — discuss challenges with your PE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special issue timing recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: Publish special issues early in a volume when possible, as they tend to exceed initial page budget estimates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scheduling special issues early helps manage page budget and avoids overspending later in the volume.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tools for tracking page usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the Quick Ref guide and SMART website for up-to-the-minute information about current and historical articles, including page counts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These tools assist in estimating page usage and tracking page budgets; ask your PE for access and help.

rubrics_metrics.name: What counts toward page budget
rubrics_metrics.description: Page budget counts editorial content plus special interior elements such as: TOC, verso (postal/copyright info), editorial board, call for papers, reviewer lists, submission guidelines, abstracts, and indexes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult your journal’s contract for additional details and costs for extra pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Production Editor (PE) role
rubrics_metrics.description: PEs are primarily project managers for the production process, guiding articles and issues through production and serving as liaison for authors, editors, and production staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PEs maintain journal-specific knowledge, review and adjust correction requests, perform quality checks, and oversee scheduling and page budgets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publishing Editor (Pub Ed) role
rubrics_metrics.description: Pub Eds are the main point of contact for journal management from manuscript submission through publication, with high-level oversight of editorial and financial health.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pub Eds provide reporting, negotiate contracts, maintain contact with journal teams, and handle contracts, finances, marketing, and other management concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sage Track capabilities and use
rubrics_metrics.description: Sage Track automates the peer-review process, can send automatic reminders and correspondence, acts as a reviewer database, and generates reports (accept/reject ratio, submission counts, time to decision, reviewer history).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sage Track (powered by ScholarOne) exports flow into SMART; editors can assign reviewer ratings and choose reviewers based on expertise using the system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sage Journals: Licensing & Payment process
rubrics_metrics.description: Sage Journals: Licensing & Payment is the platform for authors to choose and sign open access licenses, pay APCs, or sign Contributor Licenses for subscription journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are invited to the platform after acceptance; automated reminders and instructions are provided to ensure post-acceptance actions are completed to avoid production delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-acceptance transmission steps
rubrics_metrics.description: Once a manuscript is accepted in Sage Track, it must go through: (1) completion and approval of the contributor form, (2) completion of the production checklist, and (3) assignment to the production batch and export to reach production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The contributor form task is being moved to Sage Journals: Licensing & Payment over 2025; manuscripts must be assigned to the Sage Production batch and exported — contact the Peer Review Specialist for help.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental issue handling and contract requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly designate any supplement articles upon submission; articles cannot be submitted to production until the supplement contract is signed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplement material can be submitted through Sage Track or provided directly to the PE; ensure supplement contracts are in place before production.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH/PubMed Central deposit requirement for NIH-funded work
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must submit final peer-reviewed journal manuscripts arising from NIH funds to PubMed Central upon acceptance; the papers must be available on PMC no later than 12 months after publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deposit the "final accepted version" to PMC per NIH policy and consult Sage’s Green Open Access policy and the NIH/PubMed deposit website for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open access routes and obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Open access at Sage is available via Sage Gold Open Access journals, Hybrid subscription journals (Sage Choice), and Green Open Access archiving.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For Gold/Hybrid, authors request open access and pay APCs (or assign payers) through the Licensing & Payment platform; Green archiving options are covered by Sage’s archiving and sharing policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author notification at production milestones
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are notified by email when their article enters Sage production, when it has been published OnlineFirst, and when it has been published in an issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PEs can also provide PDFs by email on request; authors receive links for viewing/downloading at OnlineFirst and issue publication stages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmission troubleshooting guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: If having trouble transmitting an accepted paper from Sage Track to production, follow the listed tasks and contact the Peer Review Specialist or relevant editorial contacts for assistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify completion of contributor forms (or note transition in 2025), production checklist, and that the manuscript has been assigned to the production batch and exported.
